synthesis_top_issues.title: The 4-week MVP doesn't contain the game: no “!”, no jack-out/closing time, no progression, and the core systems have no week at all
synthesis_top_issues.flagged_by_detail: feasibility-lead (F1, BLOCKING), business-analyst (F1, BLOCKING), adversarial-qa (F3, “MVP contradiction” bullet). Systems-designer, narrative-critic and player-psychologist each added a Round 2 consequence.
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: All six reviewers engaged and none disputed it. Systems: no strategic decision or progression, so pacing can't be playtested before week 6. Narrative: zero expression of the thesis. Psych: the Construct has no build slot or final script; MVP players can only watch. Feasibility: “I know kung fu” is post-MVP by definition. Re-cut proposals converged: bridge spike, then talk plus a static “!”, with jack-in/out and closing time in the MVP; walking “!” and ragdolls deferred.

synthesis_top_issues.title: The human approval gate the safety model depends on can be forged, and the game's own rewards wear it down
synthesis_top_issues.flagged_by_detail: adversarial-qa (F2 forgeable “!”, BLOCKING; F4 autonomy dial vs. “approves every change”, MAJOR), player-psychologist (F3 approval fatigue, upgraded to BLOCKING; F5), systems-designer (F4, upgraded to BLOCKING). Connections from narrative-critic and business-analyst. Scoping caveat from feasibility-lead (C2).
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: Psych X1: habituated players approve a forged request with the same click as fifty harmless ones. Systems and QA independently found both win conditions are easiest by maxing every dial, removing the blueprint checkpoint. QA X1: no provenance, so any local process or MCP connector could post a “!” or “fed”. QA X2: the Construct's scripted worker breaks the twin rule on the first “!”. Feasibility caveat: MVP is mock-only, so this blocks connecting real accounts, not the 7-week plan; proposed gate: no real connector until ask_player carries provenance and Clerk output never feeds a keycard-holding agent.

synthesis_top_issues.title: No player except the author is designed for, and the switch from sample to real (the payoff of “real, not simulated”) has no design
synthesis_top_issues.flagged_by_detail: player-psychologist (F1, BLOCKING), business-analyst (F3, upgraded to BLOCKING), narrative-critic (F2: who is the Oracle for anyone who isn't Michael), feasibility-lead (F3: “works for Michael” vs. “ships to others”), systems-designer (F3, reframed).
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: BA X3: “Every approver in the design is Michael” — root cause behind Psych F1, Feasibility F3, and Narrative F2. Psych X3: the obvious first connectors (Gmail, iMessage) are gated or blocked, so the first real connection should be the player's own agent or local data. Systems: real loadout is paced by outside setup friction. Feasibility moved the other way, downgrading F3 to MINOR for the 7-week plan while keeping it MAJOR or worse for any real-connector release.

synthesis_top_issues.title: The bridge carries the whole design, yet it is unspecified and gets one week
synthesis_top_issues.flagged_by_detail: feasibility-lead (F2, BLOCKING). Requirements added by adversarial-qa (X1 provenance, X3 stalled state), with further dependencies traced to player-psychologist F3, systems-designer F1 and adversarial-qa F1, F4 and F5.
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: Feasibility X3 lists what colleagues now expect from the bridge: idempotency keys, ask_player provenance, presence events with no sensor source, non-visual code blueprints, cap state, and per-runtime enforcement of every autonomy-dial setting — “one week of schedule carrying most of the open problems on the board.” QA X3: a capped agent can't call ask_player, shows busy forever, never returns its keycard; needs a bridge-set “stalled” state and keycard timeout. No reviewer disputed it.

synthesis_top_issues.title: A real creature's failure or death has no truthful in-world response; the twin of a dead pet would keep saying “I'm hungry”
synthesis_top_issues.flagged_by_detail: narrative-critic (F3, upgraded to BLOCKING), adversarial-qa (F5, MAJOR; X5), player-psychologist (X6, “BLOCKING for any release beyond the author”), business-analyst (X5).
synthesis_top_issues.cross_exam_summary: Four reviewers reached the dead-pet case independently. QA X5: a dead Flora's :feed chore still counts toward “your own chores done,” forcing faked feeding or data edits while grieving. Psych X6: a grieving player returns to an overgrown estate and a hungry axolotl that no longer exists. Narrative upgraded because Flora and the snap are week 3, inside the MVP. BA changed its ask to “spec the minimal death/rehome state for live creatures in v1.” Narrative's fix: estate neglect is cosmetic and tidyable; real-creature neglect must be told truthfully in the twin's kind voice.

synthesis_just_outside_top5.title: Thesis reversed: “needing the game less” is stated but nothing in progression or the endgame delivers it
synthesis_just_outside_top5.note: Narrative corrected its evidence to credit the bedtime lock and jack-out as partial carriers. Systems and BA accepted the diagnosis but disputed the remedy (Disagreement 3).

synthesis_just_outside_top5.title: Chore events unverified, double-counted, no restock
synthesis_just_outside_top5.note: Weakened on severity, kept as a defect. Systems and Feasibility rated it a cheap local fix; Psych agreed the double count is the real BLOCKING issue and called self-report fraud out of scope; QA narrowed its core to duplicate events and unauthenticated senders. Listed as Quick Win 1.

synthesis_disagreements.title: Closing time: enforced lock or honest nudge?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_argument: Pillar 4 is the game's only differentiator from free agent dashboards; a bypassable lock plus a one-tap override makes it “a cosmetic setting.” In-fiction negotiation is fine; a free bypass is not (BA C1). The lock and jack-out are the only mechanics carrying the thesis; an override is acceptable but “never invisibly” — the world must stage it (Narrative).
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_label: Make it an honest, overridable nudge
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_argument: A hard lock on a work tool reads as software blocking your own work; frame closing time as a nudge the player authored (“you asked me to send you home”) with a cheap, explicit escape hatch (Psych C1, F4). A hard lock can't be built without revoking the player's own agent access, so the override comes for free (Feasibility X5).
synthesis_disagreements.other_positions: systems-designer: make “jacked out by bedtime” a scoring condition only, with no lock. adversarial-qa (C2): the current design annoys the complying player and does nothing to the one who doesn't; the document must choose before anything else is fixed.
synthesis_disagreements.decision_escalated: Is Prime Meridian primarily a productivity tool or a “sends you back to your life” wellness game (BA F2)? Three lenses (QA, BA, Psych) reached the same unmade decision, and the pitch must follow the answer.

synthesis_disagreements.title: Should the game ever suggest raising an agent's autonomy?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_label: Yes: a visible track record plus a suggestion
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_argument: Show each agent's history and have the twin propose raising the dial for the player to confirm, so trust is granted but no longer guessed (Systems F4). The game must say whether it ever suggests raising the dial, and careful review needs its own visible payoff (Psych F3, X2).
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_label: No agent may start a trust change
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_argument: A raise proposal arrives as a “!”, making “give me more autonomy” the most valuable request to forge. Track records can be gamed with trivial clean tasks. Show the history, but if proposals exist they must come from game code over a channel ask_player can't reach and look visibly different (QA C1).
synthesis_disagreements.decision_escalated: Who can start a trust change, and through what channel? Can't be settled until the document defines what each dial setting covers (QA F4).

synthesis_disagreements.title: What does “needing the game less” measure?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_argument: A dialogue beat can't fix an economy in which every chapter adds more “!”s. The fix must be a measured quantity designed to fall, such as “!”s per task or minutes jacked in (Systems C1 vs. Narrative F1).
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_argument: A falling “!” rate rewards agents absorbing more of the player's life; a player who hands everything to fully autonomous agents scores perfectly while becoming more dependent. It needs a human-side counterpart, such as time jacked out or chores done in person (Narrative C4 vs. Systems F4).
synthesis_disagreements.other_positions: business-analyst (C3): any engagement-priced business model conflicts with a success metric of declining use, so the thesis must also be written into the business model.
synthesis_disagreements.decision_escalated: Define the long-term win as an observable measure, decide whether it counts agent throughput, human time away, or both, and pair it with a business model that would not quietly cut it.

synthesis_disagreements.title: Write the Construct's original script now, or defer the Construct?
synthesis_disagreements.side_a_argument: Without the film lines, the Construct and Signature Moment #2 have no script; unscoped redesign of a signature moment is MAJOR (Narrative F4). “Draft the original-IP versions… now, before they are built” (BA F5, upgraded to MAJOR).
synthesis_disagreements.side_b_argument: The Construct is in no week of the schedule, so writing dialogue for an unscheduled feature spends effort before onboarding is buildable. Cut or explicitly defer it and scope the script once scheduled (Feasibility C5).
synthesis_disagreements.decision_escalated: Is the Construct v1 onboarding? If yes, the original script becomes a scheduled dependency; if not, it is deferred together with “I know kung fu.”

synthesis_quick_wins.title: Make chore events idempotent and restock manual
synthesis_quick_wins.description: Allow one completion per chore per due window (:every “2d” already defines it), restock via a manual player event in v1 (no receipt-from-mail ingestion until provenance exists), and accept SMS only from an allowlist of known senders. Reword Pillar 1 from “literally true” to “literally what you reported.”

synthesis_quick_wins.title: Replace the Construct's “every skill and MCP connector out there” rack with one curated, recommended connector
synthesis_quick_wins.description: The player's own agent or local chore data, never mail. Business-analyst X2 calls it “the best cost-to-impact cut in the document.”
synthesis_quick_wins.sourced_from_detail: business-analyst X2; addresses player-psychologist F1, adversarial-qa F2, systems-designer F3

synthesis_quick_wins.title: Commit in one line to kinematic locomotion and a static “!” marker
synthesis_quick_wins.description: Move active ragdolls and the spine swim to post-v1, and remove or explain “GPU box for physics.”

synthesis_verdict.one_line_verdict: This document is not ready to drive production.
synthesis_verdict.single_most_important_change: Re-cut the MVP so it closes the full loop against one mock worker, with a written list of what is deferred.
recommended_build_order: Bridge spike with a written event schema
strengths_credited: The moment-to-moment loop is well specified (systems-designer)
The mock-connection test rig and the “world never waits on a model” event design are sound (feasibility-lead)
synthesis_verdict.open_product_decision: Productivity tool or wellness game — sits underneath the bedtime, autonomy, and long-term-win disputes.
synthesis_verdict.full_paragraph: This document is not ready to drive production. Reviewers credited real strengths: the moment-to-moment loop is well specified (systems-designer), and the mock-connection test rig and the “world never waits on a model” event design are sound (feasibility-lead). But every lens found that the committed build does not demonstrate the game being pitched. The 4-week MVP has no “!”, no jack-out and no progression. The bridge every pillar depends on has one week and no spec. The safety model rests on a “!” that can be forged and on human attention the reward structure wears down. And the design has only ever been written for a single player, its author. The board also leaves one product decision open (productivity tool or wellness game), and it sits underneath the bedtime, autonomy and long-term-win disputes. The single change that matters most is the one all six reviewers converged on: re-cut the MVP so it closes the full loop against one mock worker, with a written list of what is deferred. The build order is a bridge spike with a written event schema, then talk with a static “!”, then answer, then approve, then the world changes, then closing time. Each of the other top issues either depends on that re-cut or is decided by it.
